steps.scene: Ahead you spot a road sign shaped like a triangle with a thick red border. You can't read the symbol inside yet.

question.prompt: Before you read the symbol, what is the triangle already telling you?

options.text: There is a hazard ahead to prepare for
You must obey an order at once
It points the way to a destination

question.explanation: The shape carries the message: a red-bordered triangle always warns of a hazard ahead. The symbol inside says which hazard.

steps.title: Crossroads ahead
steps.body: A warning triangle with a plus-shaped symbol means roads cross ahead. Traffic may pull out from either side — ease off and look both ways.

question.prompt: A warning triangle shows a plus-shaped symbol. It means…

options.text: You must give way to the right
A crossroads is ahead
The road ahead is closed

question.explanation: The plus shape stands for a crossroads ahead. It warns you roads meet; it does not set who has priority.

a.label: Plus symbol
a.body: Roads cross ahead — a crossroads. Watch left and right as you approach.

b.label: T symbol
b.body: Your road ends ahead at a junction — a T-junction. Be ready to give way.

question.prompt: A warning triangle shows a T-shaped symbol. It warns that…

options.text: Another road crosses straight over yours
Your road ends ahead at a junction
The road divides into two lanes

question.explanation: The T shape shows your road ending at a junction ahead. The plus shape, not the T, means a crossroads.

steps.title: Road narrows
steps.body: Arrows angling inward warn the road narrows ahead — on one side or both. The carriageway gets tighter, so hold back if it isn't clear.

question.prompt: A warning triangle shows arrows angling inward. What should you read from it?

options.text: The road narrows ahead, on one or both sides
The road always narrows on the right only
A lane is closed for roadworks

question.explanation: Inward arrows warn the road narrows ahead. Which side depends on the symbol — it can be one side or both.

steps.scene: A warning triangle shows a vehicle on a downward slope with a gradient figure like 10%. The road ahead drops away steeply.

question.prompt: What is the sign cueing you to do?

options.text: Pick a lower gear early so engine braking controls your speed
Hold the brakes down firmly the whole way down
Speed up to get the hill over with

question.explanation: A steep-hill-down sign warns of a sharp descent. A lower gear lets the engine hold you back so the brakes don't overheat.

steps.title: Slippery road
steps.body: A triangle with a skidding-car symbol warns of a slippery road; an 'ice' plate warns of likely ice. Grip drops, so slow down and stay smooth.

question.prompt: You see this slippery-road warning with an 'ice' plate. It tells you…

options.text: The road may be icy — slow down and brake gently
The road has been gritted, so it is safe
You must fit snow chains here

question.explanation: It warns the surface may be icy or slippery, not that it is safe. Slow down early and avoid sudden braking or steering.

steps.wrongBelief: Every warning sign tells you to do one fixed thing, like stopping.

options.text: It isn't — every warning sign means stop
Warning signs name the hazard; you choose how to respond to it
Warning signs can be ignored once you have seen them once

question.explanation: A warning tells you what is ahead. How you respond — slow, hold back, change position — depends on the hazard and conditions.

steps.repairNote: Warning signs give you information to act on, not a single order. Read the hazard, then judge the safe response.
